blocking.issue: The ADR does not say how a Node gets a trusted signing time when it verifies a keyless signature offline, so keyless verification cannot be built as written. Fulcio certificates are short-lived, so a verifier that checks them against the current time rejects every keyless signature once the certificate expires. The research records that cosign v3.1.1 moved signing to Rekor v2 with DSSE hashed entries, and that Rekor v2 is a tile-backed log. So the signing time has to come from evidence inside the Sigstore bundle (a transparency-log inclusion proof plus a trusted timestamp) that is checked against transparency-log and timestamp-authority keys in the local trusted root. The ADR requires none of this, and it names no verifier thresholds. An implementer could therefore reject every valid signature, or skip the log and weaken T6.
blocking.evidence: Decision outcome, Offline verification: "Trust roots, including the Sigstore trusted root for keyless identities, are supplied locally; Nodes never fetch one over TUF at activation." Decision table: "CI at `ruralz bundle push`, with Sigstore (keyless OIDC or a key), stored as an OCI referrer". Research (docs/_meta/research/licensing-landscape.md): "v3.1.1 (2026-06-09) made the bundle format the default and moved signing to Rekor v2 with DSSE hashed entries" and "Rekor v2 GA 2025-10-10: tile-backed log".
blocking.fix: Extend the Offline verification rule: "A keyless signature MUST be a Sigstore bundle carrying a transparency-log inclusion proof and at least one trusted timestamp. The Node checks the certificate against that time, and the log and timestamp keys against its local trusted root; a missing or unverifiable proof or timestamp is RZ-CFG-033. Key-based signatures verify against the configured key." Cite ([source](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases)) and ([source](https://blog.sigstore.dev/rekor-v2-ga/)). Add the case to the interoperability job in Confirmation: a cosign 3.1.3 keyless bundle verifies with egress denied.

blocking.issue: A Control-mode Node has no defined source for the Sigstore trusted root (Fulcio, transparency-log and timestamp keys) that it needs to verify keyless Plugin signatures at activation. The ADR says trust roots are 'supplied locally'. For Control mode, though, it names only root-signed anchor sets carrying the online keys and the Plugin trust policy. Control plane and GitOps lists the anchor set contents, and they include no Sigstore trusted root. Enrollment delivers no such root either. As written, a Control-mode Node under `enforce` either rejects every keyless-signed Plugin or needs an undocumented local file that nothing distributes or rotates.
blocking.evidence: ADR, Trust policies: "Control mode: root-signed anchor sets carry the online keys and the Plugin trust policy from Ruralz Control's process configuration, delivered at Enrollment and by `TrustUpdate`." ADR, Offline verification: "Trust roots, including the Sigstore trusted root for keyless identities, are supplied locally". 04-control-plane-and-gitops.md, Signed content: "Anchor set: `version`, `storeEpoch`, online keys, server CA fingerprint, Plugin trust policy, optional `compromisedSince`".
blocking.fix: State where the root comes from in each mode: "In Control mode the Sigstore trusted root is part of the Plugin trust policy in the root-signed anchor set, so refreshing it is a `TrustUpdate`; in file mode it comes from the Node's process configuration (OQ-security-and-identity-8)." Because Control plane and GitOps does not list it yet, cite OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-1 as the place to confirm the anchor set contents. Also add a Bad consequence: each Sigstore root refresh in Control mode needs an offline root signing.

blocking.issue: The table requires `ruralz bundle build` and `ruralz bundle validate --online` to verify Plugin signatures under `enforce`, and the ADR says an empty trust policy rejects everything. However, the ADR gives no trust policy source for the CLI. Trust policies never live in a Bundle, and the only named locations are Ruralz Control's process configuration and the Node's. The CLI reference defines no trust-policy input either. As written, every CI build of a Bundle that references a Plugin fails with RZ-CFG-033 by default, or the implementer has to invent an unreviewed input. The pack also routes CI merge gating through these commands.
blocking.evidence: Decision table, Plugin artifact row: "`ruralz bundle build`, `ruralz bundle validate --online`, Ruralz Control at ingest, Nodes at activation | `enforce`; `warn` in `ruralz dev run`". Trust policies rule: "Trust policies never live in a Bundle. Under `enforce` an empty trust policy rejects everything". 02-configuration-model.md: "CI SHOULD gate merges on `ruralz bundle build` or `validate --online`, which also verify Plugin signatures".
blocking.fix: Add to the Trust policies rule: "The CLI reads the same file-mode trust policy source as a Node (OQ-security-and-identity-8, extended to `ruralz bundle build` and `ruralz bundle validate --online`; flag names belong to [CLI and API surface](../reference/01-cli-and-api-surface.md))." Also say what happens without one: "without a trust policy the CLI fails with RZ-CFG-033 and names the missing input". Do not invent a flag.

blocking.issue: Signature discovery has no bounds. The ADR stores signatures as OCI referrers and has Nodes, Ruralz Control and the CLI find and verify them. It gives no limit on how many referrers are listed or tried, on Sigstore bundle size, or on verification time. T6 assumes an adversary who can write to the registry (tampering, retagging). That adversary can attach thousands of junk or oversized referrers to a pinned digest, so every Node that verifies spends unbounded memory and time before it reaches RZ-CFG-033. In Control mode every Node of a Cluster repeats this on the same Rollout. The owning Control plane document bounds the Ruralz Control online check (64 MiB, 30 s), but nothing bounds the Node or CLI path.
blocking.evidence: Decision table: "with Sigstore (keyless OIDC or a key), stored as an OCI referrer". Figure 1: "Full digest, then signature against local trust roots". The ADR has no limit on referrers, bundle bytes or verification time. 04-control-plane-and-gitops.md bounds only Ruralz Control: "The online Plugin check dials only allowlisted registries, binds credentials to one host, follows no redirects and stops at 64 MiB or 30 s (target)."
blocking.fix: Add a rule: "**Bounds.** Verifiers list referrers filtered by the Sigstore bundle artifact type. They try at most 16 referrers of at most 1 MiB each within 10 s (target), reusing the 64 MiB and 30 s fetch limits (target) of Control plane and GitOps. Anything beyond these limits is RZ-CFG-033. Verification results are cached by artifact digest and trust policy version." If the numbers belong to the owning document, reference them as proposed there instead.

non_blocking.suggestion: The body is about 1,492 words against the 1,500-word maximum in adr_common, so the fixes above need offsetting trims. Candidates: shorten Considered options item 1, which repeats the Decision table (keep its two citations). Merge the two P-driver bullets. Shorten the More information Research bullet to one citation pair. Do not remove text that resolved earlier findings.

Add a Bad consequence for the Key compromise rule: a Node that restarts after an emergency key removal while Ruralz Control is unreachable stays not ready. This is a deliberate exception to P9 (boot Last-Known-Good after a restart), accepted under OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-24 option (a).

Say explicitly that in Control mode the Plugin trust policy in Ruralz Control's process configuration is only the input to the offline root signing, and that Nodes honor only the root-signed anchor-set copy. As a result, revoking a Plugin publisher (listed in Security and identity as 'Next activation') waits on an offline root signing ceremony.

The stale-root consequence could say how often a refresh is needed. Rekor v2 uses yearly log shards (licensing-landscape research), so a trusted root older than a year stops verifying new keyless signatures. Consider proposing a `ruralz_node_degraded_info` reason for an aging trusted root to Observability.

verify-docs warns that line 113 ('Interoperability job, Planned (M2)') has no matching M2 roadmap item. The roadmap's M2 row says 'OCI registry integration tests and interoperability job'; reusing that wording would clear the WARN.

'What a signature binds' names a promotion signature only implicitly. Control plane and GitOps also signs promotions (Cluster, promotedDigest, storeEpoch, promotionSeq), and those signatures protect Last-Known-Good promotion from replay. Consider naming them in one clause.
